thread:
ashley: FYI onboarding HF model 'silver-lake-7b' — hit a nasty config mismatch during conversion to Redwood runtime. quantized path fails with KV cache shape errors.
ken: Can you paste the relevant bits from the HF config?
ashley: sure, here's the config snippet I saw in the repo: 
```json
{"model_type":"gpt_neox","hidden_size":4096,"num_attention_heads":32,"num_key_value_heads":16,"max_position_embeddings":2048,"rope_scaling":{"type":"linear","factor":0.8},"sliding_window":true}
```
maria: num_key_value_heads=16 but num_attention_heads=32 — that's a 2x factor which we support, but the convert tool historically expects either equal or explicit kv-head mapping. convert-bot might be normalizing it away.
convert-bot: conversion started for silver-lake-7b at commit a1b2c3. Detected rope_scaling present. Trying HF->Redwood config mapping.
ashley: on CPU-to-GPU quantized test we get this error from runtime: 
```
RuntimeError: KV cache shape mismatch: expected (batch, num_kv_heads, seq, head_dim) = (1, 32, 2048, 128) got (1, 16, 2048, 128)
During attention compute at layer 11
```
liz: That suggests the runtime applied num_attention_heads when allocating KV cache but the model wrote out num_key_value_heads into the config and convert path used that for the KV reshape. Essentially double-booking.
ken: Also rope_scaling+sliding_window combo can make effective pos indexing inconsistent during caching — sliding_window expects a fixed window and often we disable rope scaling for that mode. If rope_scaling was applied differently in HF vs Redwood, you can get off-by-window errors.
sam: Repro steps I ran: 
1) redwood convert-hf --model ./silver-lake-7b --out redwood-config.json
2) start local serving with --quantize=4bit --cache=kv
3) run short prompt > fails on first generation.
I attached the converted config (excerpt): 
```json
{"num_attention_heads":32,"num_key_value_heads":16,"kv_head_mapping":null,"max_position_embeddings":2048,"rope_scaling":{"factor":0.8}}
```
maria: `kv_head_mapping:null` is the smoking gun. Our converter should emit explicit `kv_head_mapping: [0,1,2,...]` or set `num_key_value_heads` to match attention heads when no mapping present.
ashley: Quick patch: I forced num_key_value_heads=32 in the converted config and restarted quantized serving — error goes away, generation continues but we need to validate outputs vs HF baseline for correctness (especially for long-context behavior).
liz: Good. Two followups: (1) add a converter validation that errors or auto-expands kv heads when ambiguous, (2) add a note that rope_scaling with sliding_window needs canonicalization — either rewrite rope_scaling to effective scale used by the runtime or refuse auto-conversion.
ken: Will open INF ticket for converter and add unit test for kv head mapping. Also add an eval to compare embeddings & outputs for sequences near max_position_embeddings and with sliding window enabled.
maria: For quant path, add a guard where the runtime checks allocation shape and throws a clearer error recommending num_key_value_heads parity or an explicit mapping. That will save a lot of time for oncall.
ashley: I've uploaded short eval results to the drive: small hallucination diff but overall logits align for first 512 tokens. Long-window behavior TBD.
infra-bot: Created issue INF-3245: "HF->Redwood converter: handle asymmetric KV head configs & rope_scaling+sliding_window canonicalization". Assigned to @ken.
sam: FYI I also saw one HF checkpoint that stored special token offsets differently; tokenizer roundtrip passed but chat template alignment for system messages got shifted by one when sliding_window true. Might be related.
liz: Good catch — add tokenizer smoke test to the converter pipeline: roundtrip encode(decode(system+user)) and ensure system tokens land at expected positions before applying sliding window.
ashley: Plan for now: 1) hotfix converter to coerce kv heads parity for onboarding (ashley->PR), 2) add converter validation + tests (ken), 3) add runtime guard message (maria), 4) run quant+fp32 bench and long-context eval (sam). I'll post results here. :thumbsup:
